newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Settlers clash with Palestinians in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Settlers clash with Palestinians in Hebron.

text.p: Jewish settlers and Palestinians threw stones and empty bottles at each other in Hebron on Tuesday in the Israeli-controlled area of the divided West Bank town, witnesses said.
Israeli soldiers who rushed to the area to try to stop the clashes faced hundreds of Palestinian stone-throwers. There were no immediate reports of casualties, the witnesses said.
The Israeli army said it was checking the report.

Tension between Hebron's 100,000 Palestinians and the city's 400 Jewish settlers has soared since a Jewish seminary student shot dead a Palestinian shopkeeper last week. The incident has sparked daily confrontations between Jews and Arabs in the volatile town.
Settlers clashed with Israeli police on Monday when the Israeli army tried to expand a metal gate near one of the Jewish enclaves.
Settlers, who said the new gate turns their enclave into a ghetto, hurled stones, dumped flower pots on the streets and sprayed police with water.
Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule in January. The rest of the city, where the settlers and more than 20,000 Palestinians live, remains under Israeli control.
Israel's ground-breaking on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18 touched off a wave of Palestinian unrest in the West Bank.
A suspected Palestinian militant petitioned Israel's High Court on Tuesday to prevent Shin Bet security interrogators from using "excessive force" during questioning, an Israeli court official said.

He said authorities suspected the Palestinian, identified as Ayman Qafisha, of belonging to a militant cell of the Islamic Hamas group accused of bombing a Tel Aviv cafe last month in which three Israeli women and the Arab attacker were killed.
